text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - Jordan bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. number 3 corn or better in one lot at $154.25 per tonne C and F, for first half November shipment. Jordan's Ministry of Supply made the purchase from Geneva-based Romak, traders said.

- The CCC said it would not purchase up to 16,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better yellow corn for donation to Rwanda due to program restrictions. Shipment period had been set for December 5-30. At this time, "We do not know if we will retender," a CCC official said.

SOYBEAN SALE - The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought three 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. soybeans at a tender in a range of 87.40 to 89.67 US cents/March a tonne.

- South Korea's Shindongbang Corp bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans at mixed basis prices over September and November futures on the CBOT. The shipment was set for early October from U.S. Gulf. Arrival was slated for Inchon. The purchase prices were between $325 and $330 per tonne, C and F, from a U.S. grain exporter.

WHEAT SALE - Angola bought 17,850 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the PL 480 export donation program, USDA said. The wheat was acquired from Cargill at $180.10 a tonne, FOB U.S. Gulf. Shipment was slated for October 10-October 25.

- France sold 13,000 tonnes of soft wheat and 6,570 tonnes of soft wheat flour at a food aid tender. France sold 3,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Nicaragua, a further 6,000 tonnes to Peru and another 4,000 tonnes to Bolivia at 1,130 francs per tonne, FOB Blaye. France sold 2,920 tonnes of soft wheat flour to Madagascar and 3,650 tonnes to Tanzania at 1,657 francs, FOB Toulon. The wheat and flour are for Oct 8-30 shipment.

WHEAT SALE - The Australian Wheat Board said it sold 2,000 tonnes of Australian Hard 1 for A$213 a tonne from its pools at Fremantle. Bids were submitted for 18,000 tonnnes of new crop wheat in Fremantle, Newcastle and Port Kembla. The highest failed bid was for APW wheat at A$161 per tonne, the AWB said. the closing date for the next tender is October 9.
- Turkish commodities trading and port company Toros said it was selling Iraq 14,000 tonnes of imported wheat under a U.N. aid program for Iraq.

WHEAT TENDER - Surinam will seek to purchase 2,800 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better northern spring/dark northern spring wheat in bulk under the PL 480 Title I. Shipment is set for October 10-25. Bids must be submitted by September 26.

- Pakistan will tender for 200,000 tonnes U.S.grade 2 or better soft white wheat under the GSM-102 program for October 10-31 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. Bids are due September 29 and must remain valid until September 30.
- The CCC seeks up to 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better hrw or srw or soft white wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment is set for Oct 10-Nov 5. Offers are due by Sept 26.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 is the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will decide on awarding a 50,000 tonne rice tender on Friday, the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. Forty-one exporters have responded to a Sri Lankan government tender for 50,000 tonnes of rice for October/November delivery.
- Moldova will tender Wednesday for 14,000 tonnes of PL-480 long-grain milled rice for November.

MARKET TALK - Expectations of further European Union subsidised sales and good export demand helped sustain grain prices in major European markets this week, traders said. The EU last week reverted to granting subsidies to its main grain exporters for the first time in more than a year after a bumper harvest in several areas. Subsidies had been suspended in early 1995 when world supply tightened.
